html:
SMTO-GIT-0005 — A Git settings file has a missing closing quote

GUID: f6408c0a-0b8a-4dad-a554-34869c9f8378
Slug: git-config-invalid
Domain: GIT · Subsystem: git

What happened

  • A Git settings file on the computer running the Gateway has a value with an opening quote mark but no closing one. SMTO couldn't read it, so it won't remember this project. Your Git command's result wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to run git config --list --show-origin in the project folder to see which settings file has the problem. Git names the file and line it can't read, so you know exactly where the missing quote is.
  2. Make a backup copy of that file, then open it in a text editor and add the missing closing quote mark (") to the value Git pointed to. A value is only readable when every opening quote has a matching closing quote, and the backup lets you undo a mistake.
  3. If the file is a shared one, such as /etc/gitconfig, ask the person who manages that computer to fix it instead. Shared Git settings affect every user of that computer and usually need administrator rights to change.

What success looks like

  • git config --list runs without errors, and your next Git command in that folder doesn't show this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete the settings file; it may hold your Git name, email and project addresses.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Git config parsing found an unterminated double-quoted value in a system, global, repository or worktree Git config file.

What this means

  • The bounded Git configuration value parser reaches the end while still inside a quoted value. These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.

Why this can happen

  • The bounded Git configuration value parser reaches the end while still inside a quoted value.

How to diagnose it

  • Locate the malformed value in the identified config and compare it with Git's own parser.

How to fix it

  • Run git config --list --show-origin on the Gateway host to locate the file (candidates: /etc/gitconfig or GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL or ~/.config/git/config and ~/.gitconfig, .git/config, .git/config.worktree). Back it up, then close the quoted value deliberately; SMTO does not rewrite Git configuration.
  • Inspect the named Git configuration with ordinary Git tooling and correct its quote syntax deliberately. Keep a backup before editing user configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The deliberate syntax repair is accepted by ordinary Git and bounded discovery.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
